## Why visit

One of the best matches for the combined beer, spectacular-room and food brief. The pub occupies the great hall at Gamul House: high ceilings, exposed timber, stone flooring and an unusually spacious historic room make sitting down with a pint an experience in itself. Spitting Feathers’ own beer and changing guests give it substance beyond the building. Make this a Chester meal anchor, then contrast the hall with That Beer Place’s cider selection or the Albion’s intimate traditional rooms. This is an outstanding conversion into pub use, rather than an untouched old pub interior.

## Beer

Spitting Feathers cask plus changing guest ales; official brewery page also advertises craft keg.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly documents bottled real cider; ask about current bottles rather than assume a broad draught cider range.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Freshly prepared food from King’s Kitchen is advertised by the operator; check menu, kitchen hours and availability.

## Plan the visit

Entrance involves steps up to the hall; CAMRA counts fifteen. Building-listing grades conflict within the CAMRA page, so no precise grade is asserted here.

**Getting there:** Lower Bridge Street in Chester’s historic centre, near the River Dee.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
